notes: Same structure as living-room.json, extended for two frames. Both frames share camera point PD, so ONE z-order serves both (same centre of projection). frames = the master frames in which the product is visible by design; density.not_counted lists the in-frame products that missed the (rejected) Bible 1.6 counting rule; the binding rule is Bible 1.7 S11 (D1). category = Bible 1.6 controlled vocabulary (textile, lighting, ceramics-tableware, storage-function, art-decor-toys). placement uses the product-card enum (floor, wall, window, surface, sofa, ceiling); placement_detail names the surface. z = layer order bottom to top; a product's shadow sits at z-1 unless has_shadow_layer is false. Tie-break: product layers that share a z never overlap by design (if they do, the one nearer the camera goes on top); shadow layers are multiply and order-independent; no product shares its z with a shadow layer. plan_m = position in house coordinates (docs/house-plan.json), Z from the floor. envelope_cm = maximum envelope per variant; the 3 variants stay within +-15%. hotspot and zoom_frame are set after the shell render. fillers = unsold contents (Bible 1.5), identical in all variants. set_of = each variant is a set of that many pieces. status_note marks what changed in this version.

density.rule: Bible 1.7.1 S11: minimum 14 per full-route frame is a floor; as many products as the designer judges do not detract. Counted (rule D1, 2026-10-10, with user decision D1B, 2026-10-11) = a slot whose product is >= 50% visible and covers >= 0.5% of the frame; a set counts once; fixed-product furniture counts under the same rule (D1B: here dining table, chairs and bench); not counted: neighbouring-room products, fillers, shell, fixed furniture that is not sold. A frame still short gets sold products from docs/proposals/density-after-d1.md (D1B). The counts below were estimated under the rejected 1.6 wording; the D1 counts in that proposal were measured without fixed-product: to re-measure with fixed-product counted (next clay).
